text.title: Competitor Analysis Failure Modes
text.summary: Antipatterns observed in real deployments of Competitor Analysis. Each ties a symptom to a root cause and a concrete fix. Folds in the former gotchas file: Critical agent failure modes: hallucinated numbers, pricing-page footnotes, geography drift, context overflow on 10+ competitors.

antipattern.symptom: Matrix lists only direct SaaS competitors; misses Apple Notes (indirect) and ChatGPT (future). Analysing only direct competitors and omitting indirect and future types.
antipattern.root-cause: Author over-trusted Product Hunt category filter. Indirect competitors are what customers actually use today; future competitors are the real threat in 18 months. Missing both produces a false sense of whitespace.
antipattern.fix: Force include 3-5 indirect + 2-3 future, each with sourced concrete signal.

antipattern.symptom: Snapshot stops at homepage copy; pricing footnotes and 1-star reviews unread. Surface-level analysis limited to homepage copy without digging into pricing pages, reviews, and feature documentation.
antipattern.root-cause: Author trusted marketing copy. Pricing footnotes (annual lock-in, seat minimums, transaction fees) and 1-star review themes contain more actionable signal than marketing copy.
antipattern.fix: Always fetch pricing page + G2/Capterra 1-star reviews + Reddit thread per competitor.

antipattern.symptom: Funding figures inserted without Crunchbase citation. Accepting funding figures, employee counts, or revenue estimates without a verified source.
antipattern.root-cause: Agent hallucinated plausible numbers. Without Crunchbase API access, agents invent plausible numbers. Mitigation: hard rule "if Crunchbase API unavailable, write 'unknown' — never estimate". Mark every unverified number with "(est.)".
antipattern.fix: If Crunchbase API unavailable, write 'unknown' - never estimate; mark any unverified number (est.).

antipattern.symptom: 5-star G2 score quoted as quality proof. Trusting G2 or Capterra star ratings as objective quality signals.
antipattern.root-cause: Paid placement skews stars upward; incentivised reviews under-report weaknesses. Cross-check with Reddit and Hacker News sentiment before quoting any rating.
antipattern.fix: Cross-check with Reddit + Hacker News sentiment before quoting any rating.

antipattern.symptom: Accepting a pricing number without checking effective monthly cost for 1 user billed monthly.
antipattern.root-cause: Shown price excludes annual lock-in, seat minimums, and transaction fees. Always ask "what is the effective monthly price for 1 user, billed monthly?" before accepting any pricing cell.
antipattern.fix: The Pricing dimension cell records the effective monthly cost for 1 user billed monthly, with the pricing-page URL (rule source-every-fact-cell).

antipattern.symptom: Listing 5+ future competitors with no concrete signal (job posting, acquisition, beta product).
antipattern.root-cause: Agents over-list "Google could enter here" type future competitors. Cap at 2-3 and require one concrete signal per future competitor or it inflates the threat map.
antipattern.fix: Apply rule three-competitor-types: 2-3 future competitors, each with one sourced concrete signal.

antipattern.symptom: Dumping raw scrapes from 10+ competitor websites into a single synthesis prompt.
antipattern.root-cause: Context overflows degrade gap analysis quality. Pre-summarise each competitor to the snapshot template (one Task call per competitor), then synthesise the summaries in a final pass.
antipattern.fix: Apply rule parallel-snapshot-serial-synth: one snapshot task per competitor, synthesis over the snapshots only.

antipattern.symptom: One-time analysis with no refresh schedule.
antipattern.root-cause: A competitor matrix is stale within 60-90 days. Pricing, feature flags, and team size change frequently. Schedule quarterly re-runs with the same template to produce a diff.
antipattern.fix: Book a quarterly re-run with the same snapshot template and diff against the previous matrix.

antipattern.symptom: Copying competitors' features rather than differentiating on their weaknesses.
antipattern.root-cause: Feature parity produces table stakes, not a positioning story. Your differentiation is their weakness as expressed in customer complaints.
antipattern.fix: Apply rule differentiate-on-weakness; step 5 of `content/04-procedure.xml` rejects feature-parity positioning.
